review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the main peering-trigger flow and both listed termination outcomes, but it still omits one traced requirement and contains a semantic mismatch in the malicious-request rejection path.

defects.description: Requirement R139 is still not represented in the diagram.
defects.evidence: R139 states: 'If a peered CDN provider refuses to accept user requests, a given peering arrangement ceases.' No node, edge, or final state in this module traces that provider-refusal outcome.
defects.suggested_action: Add a traced decision/termination path for provider refusal, or connect this requirement to the appropriate existing node if it is intended to be handled elsewhere.

defects.description: The policy-rejection path is modeled as rejecting the requests themselves, while the requirement says the mediator must not pass service requirements to the local PA when requests are unacceptable by provider policies.
defects.evidence: R126 says: 'If the user requests can not be accepted according the provider policies, service requirements are not passed to the local PA.' The diagram instead routes the 'no' branch from 'Requests acceptable by policy?' to 'Reject requests' and then to 'Request rejected', which changes the stated behavior from withholding service requirements to rejecting the requests.
defects.suggested_action: Revise the branch so it models non-passing of service requirements to the local PA, or rename/retarget the path only if rejection of the requests is explicitly intended by the requirement.

strengths: Covers the core trigger sequence: content request, hotspot generation, initialization request, mediator receipt.
Includes both required termination outcomes for this module: accepted and cancelled/rejected.
Uses the required actor lanes for End-user, Web Server, and Mediator.
unsupported_behaviors: Rejecting the user requests on the basis of provider-policy acceptance is not stated by R126; the requirement only says service requirements are not passed to the local PA.
